<reason>The debate turned on one decisive question that A successfully made central: once you strip the payment toll, who funds the security infrastructure ("baseline standards") that must still exist? A's opening dilemma (either baseline standards recreate app review or they're too loose to stop fraud) was called a "false dilemma" by B, but when B specified the baseline (signed identity, malware scanning, kill-switch revocation) and the funding model ("pay for what you use," "modest developer fees," a browser safe-browsing analogy), A's Rebuttal 2 landed a clean counter-punch: this is app review's core functions, recreated, but now funded by an underspecified mechanism that doesn't capture the externality of fraud (a rogue store skipping security doesn't bear the full cost of harm it causes ecosystem-wide). B never gave a concrete answer to who specifically pays for OS-level enforcement once the fee is gone, leaving "modest developer fees" as an assertion rather than a mechanism. A's "kitchen, not inspector" reframe of B's food-safety-inspector analogy, and its turn of B's own open-web fraud comparison against them, were sharper and more original than B's largely conventional monopoly-rent framing. B's strongest unaddressed point — that current "choice" is already punished via anti-steering rules and outright iOS bans — was met by A's camouflage argument rather than squarely refuted, but A's closing crystallized the "who pays" gap more convincingly than B's closing crystallized a funding answer. Both sides handled the Pressure Questions format correctly with proper A1/A2 labeling, but A's answers exploited B's vagueness more effectively than B's answers exploited A's dilemma-framing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 2 (A4.3–A4.5), which took B's own specified "baseline standard" (signed identity, malware scanning, kill-switch revocation) and showed it was OS-maker infrastructure that must still be built platform-wide while B's "pay for what you use" model leaves the externality of fraud unfunded — directly answering A's own pressure question and never fully resolved by B's closing.</best_rebuttal>
